summary.name: LiteEdit
summary.one_liner: A lightweight, native macOS code editor under 1 MB, built with Swift and AppKit, for quickly opening a repo, making small edits, and moving on.
use_cases: quickly read code in a cloned project
edit YAML, JSON, or env config values
keep a scratch or notes editor beside an IDE
fast edits on large files with 100k+ lines
browse a project folder tree without an IDE
summary.what_it_does: LiteEdit is a native macOS code editor written in Swift and AppKit, described as under 1 MB with no Electron. It opens folders with a sidebar folder tree, and supports tabs, Cmd+P fuzzy file search, and Find & Replace with regex. It provides syntax highlighting for 20+ languages using viewport-based lazy highlighting, and Cmd+Shift+L selects all occurrences for multi-cursor editing. It also restores folder, open tabs, cursor positions, scroll position, and window state across restarts.
notable: Native Swift and AppKit build under 1 MB, with no Electron
Viewport-based lazy syntax highlighting for very large files
Installable via Homebrew Cask or built from source
caveats: Building from source requires Xcode CLI Tools
